module_title: Windows and Browser Shortcuts - Foundational Basics
introduction: In competitive exams, keyboard shortcuts are factual 'rote memorization' questions. This foundational level covers the absolute basic Windows OS and Web Browser shortcuts that are universally used and frequently tested in Tier-1 exams.

core_concepts.title: The Universal Text Shortcuts
core_concepts.description:
- `Ctrl + C`: Copy
- `Ctrl + X`: Cut
- `Ctrl + V`: Paste
- `Ctrl + Z`: Undo the last action
- `Ctrl + Y`: Redo an undone action
- `Ctrl + A`: Select All items/text.

core_concepts.title: Basic App Navigation
core_concepts.description:
- `Alt + Tab`: Switch between currently open applications or windows.
- `Alt + F4`: Close the active item, or exit the active application.

core_concepts.title: Basic Browser Shortcuts
core_concepts.description:
- `Ctrl + T`: Open a new Tab.
- `Ctrl + N`: Open a completely new Window.
- `Ctrl + W` (or `Ctrl + F4`): Close the current Tab.

core_concepts.title: The Start Menu
core_concepts.description: - `Win` (Windows Key) or `Ctrl + Esc`: Open the Windows Start Menu.

important_entities.name: Alt + F4 vs. Ctrl + W
important_entities.significance: `Alt + F4` is a system-level command that kills the entire software application. `Ctrl + W` only closes the active document or browser tab while keeping the software running.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Aspirants sometimes mistakenly associate 'Paste' with `Ctrl + P`. Remember, `Ctrl + P` is universally used for **Print**. Paste is strictly `Ctrl + V`.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Notice your keyboard: Z, X, C, and V are right next to each other on the bottom left. They represent the chronological order of fixing mistakes: Undo (Z), Cut (X), Copy (C), and Paste (V).

exam_strategy_tips: For basic level exams, if a question asks how to switch between active apps, immediately look for `Alt + Tab`. It is one of the most repeated questions in computer awareness.
